sentences.text: The claimant, is a nine year old boy attempting to cross the road near Venkata Krishna Road on 23.01.2019 at about 15.30 hours.

At https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1179 of 2024 that time, the driver belonging to the Tranport corporation drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and he hit the minor.

As a result of which, the minor sustained the following injuries :-
Grade III B compound injury with physical injury head of PPT and base of 2nd toe left foot.

sentences.text: 2. The minor underwent treatment as an inpatient for nearly 15 days and he underwent surgery.
The Medical board assessed the disability at 20%.
It is under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed by the minor represented through his mother and next friend seeking for payment of compensation against the Transport Corporation.

3. The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence came to a conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the bus belonging to the Transport Corporation.

4. Having rendered such a finding, the Tribunal proceeded to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1179 of 2024 fix the compensation and the total compensation was fixed at Rs.1,76,036/- under various heads as follows :-

undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomforts etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 2.

Medical expenses Rs. 8,536/-

6.

Total Rs.1,76,036/-
 Rounded off to  Rs.1,76,100/-
The above compensation was directed to be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.
5. The claimant not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation fixed by the Tribunal has filed this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: This Court carefully considered the submissions made on either side and the materials available on record.
8. This Court also carefully went through the award passed by the Tribunal.

9. The crux of the arguments that was projected on the side of the appellant is that the medical board had assessed the permanent disability at 20% and the Tribunal by considering the judgement of the Apex Court in Master Mallikarjun case reported in 2014 14 SCC 396, reduced the disability percentage to 10% and fixed the compensation at Rs.1,50,000/- and this was contended to go against the judgement of the Apex Court, which was relied upon by the Tribunal.

It was further submitted that the claimant had undergone treatment as an in patient for nearly 15 days and was also operated and therefore, the compensation https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1179 of 2024 fixed under the head of extra nourishment and attender charges is on the lower side and it requires enhancement.
10.

The 1st issue is with regard to the finding of the Tribunal reducing the disability percentage as 10% on the ground that the nature of injury sustained by the minor is with respect to the left lower limb and therefore, the whole body disability was fixed at 10%.
11.
The Apex Court in Mallikarjun case, referred supra has considered as to how compensation has to be fixed for children suffering from disability on account of motor vehicle accident.
While undertaking this exercise, the Apex Court held that if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000/- can be fixed as compensation.
12. In the instant case, the Medical Board had assessed 20% permanent disability.
The Tribunal had reduced the disability to 10%.

The nature of injuries sustained by the minor is such that there is total disfiguration of the left foot and the left foot for all practical purposes will remain to be a permanent disability for the minor.

When the Apex Court https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1179 of 2024 spoke about the disability to the whole body, the Courts must take into consideration the severity of the injury sustained by the minor.
The Courts should not be giving a literal interpretation that the disability must be all over the body.

The extent of injury sustained on the left foot will certainly impact the movement of the minor and the same was taken into consideration by the Medical board, which fixed the permanent disability at 20%.

In view of the same, this Court is inclined to grant a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- as compensation for the disability suffered by the minor.
13.
The minor had undergone treatment for nearly 15 days as an inpatient and a surgery was also performed.
Therefore, this Court is inclined to increase the compensation under the Head of Extra Nourishment to Rs.15,000/-and attender charges to Rs.10,000/- .

14. In the light of the above discussion, this Court modifies the compensation in the following manner:

Compensation awarded under Amount No. the head (in Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings already Rs.3,00,000/-
undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomforts etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 2.

Medical expenses Rs. 8,536/-
3.

Transportation expenses Rs.5,000/-
4.

Nutrition expenses Rs.15,000/-
5. Damages to clothes Rs.1,000/-
6.

Attender Charges Rs.10,000/-
 Total Rs.3,39,536/
 Rounded off t  Rs.3,39,600/
15.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.1,76,100/- is enhanced to Rs.3,39,600/-.

The Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation, less the amount already deposited, together with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment.
Insofar as the enhanced compensation is concerned, the deficit court fee, if not paid, shall be paid by the appellant.
The other https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1179 of 2024 directions issued by the Tribunal with regard to the mode of payment of compensation
remains unaltered.
In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed in the above terms.
No costs.
